title: Chapter 28 — The City Beneath the City

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 28
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The City Beneath the City
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They did not return to the plaza, and the City did not force them to.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Instead it simply rearranged the streets until every corridor they chose led back to the same narrow alcove. Zeek noticed the first repetition when he saw the cracked tile under the covered walkway for the second time. BAH-lahg noticed it when the same dripping water resumed its patient count. NEEN-soon stopped writing after the third return and simply stared at the wall as though the stone itself had insulted her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man who had refused still sat where they had left him, knees drawn up, humming under his breath. He did not look surprised to see them again.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: You tried the eastern passage,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said. It was not a question.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's axe rested across his shoulders.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: We are walking in circles.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: No,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the man answered.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: You are being returned. Circles would be kinder.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo's knife was already in her hand.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: How many times does it do this?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man smiled with half his mouth.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: Until you stop trying to leave the way you came, or until you decide the price of staying is lower than the price of another attempt. Most people choose the second option before the fifth return.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down the narrowing street they had just walked. The geometry had already begun to shift again; the far end no longer matched the memory of the last attempt. The mark under the linen on his palm pulsed once, slow and deliberate, as if confirming a ledger entry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They tried a fourth time anyway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This passage led behind the low wall of inventories and down a slope that grew colder with every step. The air tasted of iron and old paper. For several minutes the City allowed them the illusion of progress. Then the floor leveled, the walls widened, and the same alcove waited at the end of the corridor. The man was still humming.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg lowered the axe and sat on the paving stones without ceremony.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I don't like this place.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: That is sensible,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the man said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I wasn't asking.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: The living rarely do.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon had already moved to the long panel of wedge marks that ran along the wall opposite the alcove. She brushed dust from the deepest lines with careful fingers. The torchlight sank into the oily stone and did not return.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: These are older than the household inventories,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Different hand. Different purpose.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stepped closer. The mark on his palm had begun to warm in a way that no longer felt like warning. It felt like recognition.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon's stylus hovered above the first line.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The root forms are familiar. Settlement. Binding. Debt. But the combinations refuse ordinary translation. The first line could mean discovered. Or summoned. Those are not the same thing.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: No,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She continued, voice growing quieter.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The people who sealed the upper city did not build what lies beneath it. The earliest records claim the first settlers entered from above and found roads, wells, storage chambers already waiting. They believed the place had been abandoned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked at the man in the alcove.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: By whom?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon's finger stopped on a character whose edges had eroded.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The word can mean inhabitants. It can also mean remains. Echoes. The dead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man gave a dry, unused laugh.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I preferred it when we were only lost.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo's eyes stayed on him.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You know this language.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I know what it cost.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon forced herself farther along the wall. The next section was more formal, the wedges deeper and more carefully arranged. Phrases repeated with bureaucratic insistence: the agreement, the binding, the debt below.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Debt is not exact,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Obligation. Price. Something owed to the foundation.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek studied the spiral-drop that appeared among the characters.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You once told me it was a royal emblem.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I was wrong.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon's voice had gone flat.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It is a claim of ownership. Not chosen. Assigned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man in the alcove spoke before she could continue.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I know what it means when the mark chooses someone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek turned.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Then say it.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: You would not believe me.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Try.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man's cloudy eyes held his.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: You are already doing what your father did. He believed knowing the truth would make him free of it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words landed with the weight of an unpaid account. Zeek said nothing. He had spent twelve years carrying the shape of that belief; hearing it spoken by a stranger did not make it lighter.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon reached the final section. The characters here had been cut with force rather than patience. Several surrounding blocks were cracked. She read the first line once, then again, then stopped breathing.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: What does it say?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She looked at Zeek. Whatever he saw in her face drained the last of the anger from his expression.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The First City was not the first city.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Silence settled over the alcove the way dust settles after a collapse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then the stone moved.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A thin groove appeared beneath the final line and carved itself into the black rock without tool or hand. Another line formed beside it. Then another. The City was writing—or correcting.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon translated as the words appeared.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The first city was built over the second.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A new line.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The second was built over the third.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her breathing quickened.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The third was built over the—

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stepped closer.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Over what?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon stared at the final symbol.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The word is present. But there is no place beneath it. No chamber. No city. No depth. Nothing the language is willing to name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man in the alcove spoke softly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: Do not ask what lies beneath the last city.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek turned.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first time the man's composure cracked. His eyes shifted toward the darkness beyond the alcove, and something that resembled genuine fear moved across the wasted face.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: Because it may hear you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first knock sounded from somewhere beyond the chamber.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three measured strikes. Not loud. Not hurried. The sound traveled through the black stone without echoing, through the soles of their feet and the bones of their bodies.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon turned slowly toward Zeek. He was staring at his left hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath the linen pulsed—not with his heartbeat. The spiral and the drop had darkened until they were almost black. Beneath the symbol the flesh of his palm began to rise. A thin line appeared under the skin, pushing upward from somewhere deeper than muscle or bone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then the line moved.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A single knock sounded against the inside of his palm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man closed his eyes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon's voice dropped to a whisper.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The knocks are not coming from the walls anymore.
lines.note: Whispered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Then where?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She pointed at his hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark knocked again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This time the answer came from far below the City—faint at first, easily mistaken for settling stone or the ordinary shifting of ancient foundations. Then it came again. Three measured strikes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: From somewhere beneath them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's face had gone completely still.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man opened his eyes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And somewhere far below the First City, something knocked back.
